$comment: What each broker's public terms say about benchmarking, publication and use of its name, read before this site names a broker next to a measured number. scripts/provider-terms.mjs (run at the end of scripts/build.mjs) refuses the build of a page that does so unless the broker's entry has benchmarking 'allowed', a name use of 'plain-text' or 'plain-text-only', no open founder review, and an accepted read. Accepted reads: 'human' always; 'agent-browser-verbatim' (a headless browser rendered the page and the quote is copied from that text) only with the sha256 of the text that was read. No entry here is a human read yet; the lab owner can change readBy to 'human' after reading the page. This is a record of what the pages say, not legal advice: a clause that is unclear is quoted and left to the lab owner, not interpreted.
readMethod: Each page was rendered on 2026-10-23 with a headless Chromium (odin-labs .claude/scripts/playwright-isolated.mjs, one fresh browser context per page) and its document.body.innerText was saved. textSha256 is the sha256 of that UTF-8 text. The text was searched for benchmark, competitive, comparative, publicity, publish, trademark, trade name, logo and endorse, and every hit in the terms body was read in context. scripts/provider-terms-capture.mjs repeats the read and reports, per provider, the hash and whether every quoted passage is still on the page. A quote is verbatim: passages are joined by ' [...] ', and a 'no clause found' quote cites its closest clause between single quotes. A second read with that script on 2026-10-23 reproduced the recorded hash exactly for OpenRouter and Doubleword; the EUrouter, Requesty and orq.ai texts hashed differently (their page chrome renders differently from one load to the next), and every quoted passage was found on all five pages.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.quote: no clause found: the terms body has no benchmarking, comparison or name-use clause; publicity appears only as a third-party right of publicity that user inputs must not infringe. The closest prohibited use: 'access the Site or Service for purposes of reselling API access to Models or otherwise developing a competing service'

eurouter.name: EUrouter

founderReview.reason: The clause names 'trade names' as well as trademarks and branding. Whether a factual mention of the name next to a measurement needs consent is left to the lab owner.

eurouter.quote: The Customer shall not: (a) reverse-engineer, decompile, or disassemble the API or any part of the Service infrastructure; (b) use the Services to develop a product or service that directly competes with EUrouter; (c) remove or alter any proprietary notices or labels on the Services; or (d) use EUrouter’s trademarks, trade names, or branding without EUrouter’s prior written consent.

requesty.name: Requesty

founderReview.reason: Section 13.1 bars systematically collecting Requesty's 'model performance data, benchmarks, or routing intelligence for competitive purposes'. Measuring our own calls is not obviously that, but a recurring public broker comparison could be read as it. Left to the lab owner.

requesty.quote: You must not: [...] extract, scrape, or systematically collect our proprietary model performance data, benchmarks, or routing intelligence for competitive purposes;

orq.name: orq.ai
orq.quote: no clause found: no benchmarking, publication or name-use clause. The closest restriction, item (vi): 'not use the Services to develop, train or improve models that compete with the Services (except to the extent such restriction is not permitted by Applicable Law);'

doubleword.name: Doubleword
doubleword.quote: use the Service for benchmarking or competitive analysis intended to compare the Service with a competing offering, except with our prior written consent; [...] use our name, trademarks, or branding, or refer to us or the Service, in a way that could reasonably imply endorsement, affiliation, or sponsorship without our prior written consent.
